text:
maya: Heads-up — CI on main is failing the integration TLS tests (gRPC handshake errors) after the base image libssl bump. Last green was at commit d4e9f7a (1887654000). Can someone help bisect or confirm culprit?

ci-bot: job: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/33721 — failing task: integration/tls. Latest log excerpt:
```
E 2026-03-08T14:52:12.345Z grpc: handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: EOF
E 2026-03-08T14:52:12.346Z rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed"
```

sam: is this happening on all builders or a subset?

ops-bot: only repro on build-fleet/linux-gke-optimized. macOS and windows lanes are green.

liam: I can take this. Quick Q: do we know the base image tag that got bumped and the exact package change?

maya: yes — base image rwinf/base:2026-03-01-ab12 -> rwinf/base:2026-03-09-bump-openssl. The package bump was openssl 1.1.1 -> openssl 3.1.0 in the image. The Dockerfile line changed to:
```
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y libssl-dev=3.1.0-1
```

liam: thanks. Plan: reproduce locally with linux-gke build image, run the failing integration tests against the pinned service. I'll try a quick binary search by swapping base image tags in the dockerfile. Steps I'll run: 
```
git checkout main
git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad d4e9f7a HEAD
# iterate: edit Dockerfile to pin rwinf/base:<candidate-tag>, then docker build & run tests
# example local test:
docker build -t rwinf/integration-test:bisect . && docker run --rm rwinf/integration-test:bisect ./run_integration.sh --filter tls
```

sam: if this is openssl API/protocol change, a quick mitigation is to pin the base image to the older tag in CI while we investigate (fast revert). That would get main green asap.

maya: agreed — do we have an existing revert PR template? If liam confirms culprit we can open a revert right away.

liam: starting bisect now on a small range (2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-09). Will try two candidates in parallel to speed up. If I hit the failure locally I'll dump full openssl error with s_client.

liam: quick debug command I run to reproduce handshake errors against service endpoint: 
```
openssl s_client -connect localhost:50051 -servername api.service.local -tls1_2
```

ci-bot: rerun queued for the linux-gke-optimized lane (pragmatic re-run to gather more artifacts).

sam: if bisect points to openssl 3.x, we should also try building with BoringSSL (if supported) to see if gRPC change is the issue or the system libs.

maya: noted. Also pinging security team privately to see if any TLS policy changes were pushed in the infra account.

ops-bot: FYI: the node image has a kernel-level NetworkPolicy plugin update on 2026-03-07 but that shouldn't affect TLS handshakes — just in case.

liam: quick update — built candidate with rwinf/base:2026-03-05 and tests still fail. Built with rwinf/base:2026-03-02 (older) and tests pass. Looks like the range is small. Continuing bisect.

maya: excellent — if you get a reproducible commit, please open a revert PR and tag me + @sam so we can fast-track CI revert and run full matrix.

liam: will do. I'll post the bisect verdict and minimal reproducer (log + Dockerfile diff) in this thread. ETA ~30–60m.

sam: thanks liam :thumbsup: — LMK if you want me to open the revert PR while you prepare logs (I can open a pin to rwinf/base:2026-03-02).

liam: one more note: if someone needs to debug quickly, set the env var GRPC_TRACE=all GRPC_VERBOSITY=DEBUG in the test runner to get more handshake detail.

maya: awesome. will wait for the bisect result before escalating.

liam: starting the parallel builds now — will update soon.
